messages:
Alinor: Heads up — ACME pilot asked for an "instant-suggest" flow that matches CompetitorX's surface experience. They specifically called out: suggestions while typing, sub-100ms perceived latency, and zero regressions on hallucination. They want this in the pilot window (≈6 weeks). Can we scope?

Divya: Do we know whether ACME means feature parity (matching internal ranking/UX) or just perceived parity (fast, acceptable quality)? :thinking:

Sasha: Short answer: perceived parity is doable quickly with a light-weight model + aggressive caching. True feature parity (same ranking + reranking signals) is a larger lift — needs feature parity dataset + rerank model. Cost/infra note: naive approach increases token cost ~25–40% and requires hot KV caches on dedicated nodes.

Carmen: OK — propose 2-path plan: 1) MVP (perceived parity) scoped for pilot, 2) Post-pilot work to close ranking parity if ACME converts. MVP details inlined below.

Carmen: MVP (suggested acceptance criteria):
```
- Frontend: incremental suggestions enabled, debounce 50ms
- Backend: lightweight suggestion model (quantized 4-bit) with prefix KV cache
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end < 200ms in US-WEST under pilot load
- Quality: suggestion precision >= baseline - 5% on ACME prompt set
- Cost: per-request token cost delta <= +20% vs baseline route
- Safety: no increase in high-severity hallucination alerts over baseline
- Rollout: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on errors
```

Alinor: Good list. Sasha — can infra meet the KV-hot requirement within 6 weeks? If not, we need a fallback plan.

Sasha: We can for 6 weeks if we use burst-dedicated pool + prewarm script, but ops will want a short runbook. Risk: prewarm bumps spend. Estimate: $Xk/mo for pilot (ballpark). I can write the prewarm cron and monitoring dashboard.

Divya: For metrics, let's capture: per-route latency P95, suggestion CTR, suggestion precision (manual eval on 1000 pairs), and hallucination rate (automated heuristics). Also log model-variant tag for attribution.

Carmen: Rollout plan: canary for 1 hour at 1%, then monitor metrics for 24h. If any metric breaches threshold -> rollback. We'll use the per-route dashboard (link: https://redwood.internal/console/routes/instant-suggest) and create an eval set named acme-instant-v1.

Sasha: Will add a feature flag + fast fallback to baseline model if latency > target. Implementation note: use async prefix caching and keep sync path to baseline for the first 50 chars typed.

Alinor: Sounds good. Action items: Carmen to draft MRD + acceptance criteria, Sasha to prototype prewarm + flag, Divya to prepare eval set. @eng-bot please create ticket for "acme-instant-mvp" in the product backlog. :rocket:

eng-bot: Created ticket RW-4721 "acme-instant-mvp" assigned to Carmen, Sasha, Divya. Estimated sprint: next iteration.
